record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some results are presented only in figures, so their numerical values are not stated in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures the structure and interpretability of SAE features using methods different from the toy-network superposition experiments.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports reconstruction and cross-entropy gains for Tokenized SAEs. Those comparisons do not themselves measure the claim's feature-geometry versions, so they are not rows. The text describes several figure-based trends without numerical values.
record.test_reason: The paper measures what GPT-2 SAE features encode. It reports that many reflect training-token frequency statistics, and that the feature set shifts with SAE size and with adding a token lookup table. These results bear on whether dictionary features are canonical, stable units of the model (V5). The SAE is not used merely as a tool here.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that training-token imbalance makes many SAE features (e.g. RES-JB) reconstruct common n-grams, so these features reflect input statistics. A per-token lookup bias (Tokenized SAE) frees features for more complex, context-dependent content. It also improves reconstruction in sparse regimes (about 25% sparser at equal reconstruction) and trains 6–10x faster. Feature-quality evidence is preliminary.
record.recipe_differences: This is an empirical study and method proposal about sparse autoencoders and token reconstruction, not the toy-network feature-superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature patterns vary with SAE size: smaller SAEs lack capacity for individual or small token sets, medium SAEs show features representing multiple tokens, and larger SAEs show features for specific tokens. Tokenized versus non-tokenized SAE construction also changes the unigram and n-gram feature measurements.

fits_no_version.finding: Residual activations lie close to unigram residuals, and the final-token unigram is often nearest, across models and layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: LLM residual streams contain a strong last-token subspace.

fits_no_version.finding: In GPT-2 small, a three-token suffix approximates hidden representations across the network.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local context approximates latent representations even in deep layers.

record.problems: The authors describe the manual feature study as limited in sample size and preliminary. Several quantitative feature comparisons are shown only in figures without numerical values. The paper says a more thorough study of Tokenized SAE dictionary and lookup-table feature quality remains to be done.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep or geometry analysis.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or capacity-allocation test.
The study uses SAEs on GPT-2 but does not test whether features are spread across neurons or whether sparse model features exist and are recovered.
Completeness of the dictionary and agreement across random seeds are not tested. Only dependence on training statistics, SAE size and architecture is tested.

missing.what: A minority of layer-8 GPT-2 SAE features respond to none of the 212K most common n-grams (n≤6). Qualitatively, these features are more semantic. No count is given.
Qualitative categorisation of the first 25 top-k TSAE layer-8 features (thematic, skipgram, inductive, etc.), for comparison with RES-JB Table 3.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked everything to V4, but the paper never tests whether sparse features exist in LLMs; it uses SAEs and examines what they learn. Its bearing is on V5, since features depend on data frequency, dictionary size and architecture. Several V5 rows are the authors' own architecture comparisons, and the manual scores rest on 20 features. Most quantitative trends are figure-only. The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No toy networks, overcomplete sparse-feature sweep, near-orthogonal geometry, or sparsity-dependent transition is tested.
The study does not test polysemantic neurons, competition between model features for neuron dimensions, or allocation according to feature importance.
The study does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
The paper studies SAE features and token-related structure, not whether features are spread across many neurons or whether an SAE dictionary recovers all relevant features.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across settings, or canonical units of the model.
The study does not compare one-dimensional feature directions with multidimensional features.
